Classify a pedon under the German KA5 soil systematics (2005)

Source: R/key-ka5.R
classify_ka5.Rd

Keys a PedonRecord to the divisions (Abteilungen), classes (Klassen) and types (Typen) of the German soil systematics of the Bodenkundliche Kartieranleitung, 5th edition (Ad-hoc-AG Boden 2005, KA5), by its key Tab. 51. Experimental: this release keys the 4 divisions, 21 classes and 56 types, and the 223 subtypes of the type texts (pp. 202-262: 138 of the terrestrial types, 85 of the semiterrestrial, subhydric and Moore types), and the varieties and subvarieties of Tab. 46-50 (pp. 263-282).

Usage

classify_ka5(
  pedon,
  rules = NULL,
  on_missing = c("warn", "silent", "error"),
  gapfill = FALSE
)

Arguments

pedon

A PedonRecord.

rules

Optional pre-loaded rule set (load_rules("ka5")).

on_missing

One of "warn" (default), "silent", "error".

gapfill

Opt-in within-pedon gap-fill, as in classify_usda.

Value

A ClassificationResult with system_id "ka5": the deepest class assigned in name, the division in rsg_or_order, the division, class and type in levels, the key trace, and provisional_because.

Details

The subtypes (Hugo's decision Q21): inside a type the transitional subtypes (X-Y, a subtype of the type Y with the features of X) are tested first in printed order, then the deviation subtypes in printed order, the Norm subtype last as the fallback; the first that passes names the subtype, and every subtype of the type that passes is listed in trace$subtypes_passing. Each subtype is one of its printed formulas matched on the horizons (match_horizon_sequence), its depth windows from the GOF and its numbers (base saturation, clay differences, Cp/Fep, slope ...). The Rigosol and the Treposol take an open subtype in brackets for the type still recognisable under the R ("[BB-YY]", Q22); the Treposol has no Norm subtype, the Moorgley neither (an uH over a Gr takes the open "[Uebergangsmoorgley]", an hHm under the Erdhochmoor the open "[vermulmtes Erdhochmoor]").

The varieties (Hugo's decision Q1): an additive level after the subtype, rows of level "variety" in levels (the code of Tab. 49 with the digit of its subvariety, the word of the name, the gloss, the full symbol in a symbol column). A variety is offered where Tab. 50 marks the subtype, plus the six of its note 1 (og, c, z, k, v, ku) everywhere; each criterion of Tab. 46 is read on the horizons (the symbols written, or the recorded data), the humus forms only as recorded; one the data leave open is not named but listed in trace$varieties. The name becomes the full name (adjectives before the subtype's name, nouns in brackets before its deciding part: "podsolige Normbraunerde", "(Acker)Gley"), the symbol (rules I-VII: pBBn, g4.p2BBn, BB-rGG) is in trace$variety$symbol. The further subtypes of the type that pass join as a combination (Tab. 46 no. 17; Q21: PP-GG-BB, GGh-GGc).

The overlays (Tab. 46 no. 18) are reported in trace$overlay and the warnings, and enter the name as a variety (YK/BB, Kolluvisol ueber Braunerde); the levels above it do not change. A mineral cover on a Moor keeps the Moor (Hugo's decision Q7): under 2 dm it is named as substrate only, 2 to < 3 dm "flach X ueber HN" (X\HN), 3 to < 4 dm "X ueber HN" (X/HN), the cover keyed as the mineral type it would be. A fersiallitic or ferrallitic palaeosol (a relict or fossil Bj or Bu) under the soil is named "... ueber Fersiallit / Ferrallit" (Q19); a buried soil (fossil horizons of a layer II or deeper) is keyed alone from its own top and named by the thickness of the soil above (under 3 dm "flach", 3 to < 7 dm; 7 dm or more the upper soil alone).

The key reads the horizons of the profile (identify_horizons(pedon, "ka5")): the KA5 notation where the profile is written in it (declared with site$designation_system = "ka5", or recognised by a sign only it writes: the degree sign, a lower-case prefix before a master such as lC, fAh, aM, tmGo, Sw, Sd, Axh, Bfv ...), otherwise soilKey's order of tests on the recorded data. The last symbol of a designation carries the horizon (Bv-Go is a Go, Go-Bv a Bv). Depths are read from the GOF, the top of the first horizon that is not L, O, Of, Oh or Ovh (p. 79). The order and gates are Tab. 51's (the Moore, the subhydric soils, the semiterrestrial soils, the terrestrial soils), with the numbers of the type texts where the compressed key differs and two rules of the figures Abb. 22 and 23 (Hugo's decisions Q5 and Q6). A gate the data leave open makes the result provisional (provisional_because); a type that holds only on the designation, a measurement missing (the Fahlerde without its clay, C13), or by the key's order with the record missing (the Rigosol without the kind of deep cultivation, Q23), is listed there too.

Names as printed (German) in name and levels$name, with soilKey's English gloss in levels$name_en. The horizon panel (one row per layer: depths from the GOF, the horizon read, the route notation, data or both, the candidates, the evidence) is in trace$horizon_panel, the full frame in trace$horizons, the consistency flags of the figures in trace$figures. The readings where the text is silent are listed in system.file("rules", "ka5", "readings.yaml", package = "soilKey").

References

Ad-hoc-AG Boden (2005). Bodenkundliche Kartieranleitung. 5. Auflage. Bundesanstalt fuer Geowissenschaften und Rohstoffe, Hannover.

See also

make_ka5_example, identify_horizons, soilkey_systems.

Examples

res <- classify_ka5(make_ka5_example("BB"), on_missing = "silent")
res$name
#> [1] "Normbraunerde"
res$levels
#>       level           code                name             name_en
#> 1 divisions [terrestrisch] Terrestrische Böden   Terrestrial soils
#> 2   classes              B          Braunerden        Brown earths
#> 3     types             BB           Braunerde         Brown earth
#> 4  subtypes            BBn       Normbraunerde Typical brown earth
